question: Ophthalmological ointments:

options.opa: They may contain solid particles but only with a controlled size.
options.opb: They do not need to be sterile.
options.opc: They require the test of pyrogens.
options.opd: They can not be W / O emulsions.
options.ope: Always your excipients must be fatty

analysis: Ophthalmological ointments are required to be sterile to prevent any risk of infection when applied to the eyes. They may contain solid particles, but these particles must be carefully controlled in size to avoid irritation to the eyes. The requirement for testing of pyrogens is essential to ensure the safety of the product. Ophthalmological ointments can be formulated as water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, providing benefits such as increased ocular residence time.
